title: Philidor Defence | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: We take White and open e4, Black meets e5.
Black plays d6 — the Philidor, not a Four Knights.
The way to get an edge against the Philidor is to strike the centre with d4.
Black takes on d4.
We recapture with the knight, with better control of the centre.
Black develops the knight to f6 and we bring ours to c3.
Black develops the bishop to e7. There are several good setups — the bishop to f4 with the queen to d2 — but a nastier one that flies under the radar is to fianchetto with g3.
We play g3 — the fianchettoed bishop and the e4-pawn team up to make it very hard for Black to break with ...d5.
Black castles.
We complete the fianchetto with the bishop to g2.
Black plays the classic ...c5 — but it's a positional error: it leaves the d6-pawn backward and, above all, weakens the d5-square. Now, where should our knight go? We want it working efficiently.
The knight to f5 allows ...Bxf5, a trade I don't want, so we play the knight to e2 — from there it heads to f4 to control d5.
Black develops the knight to c6.
No need to rush the knight to f4 — first we complete development and castle.
Black pins with the bishop to g4.
We play h3 to chase the bishop — f3 would work but we'd rather not weaken ourselves.
Black captures on e2.
We recapture with the knight, not the queen — the queen would walk into ...Nd4 with tempo. And we still deny ...d5: we hold three defenders against two attackers on that square.
Black plays the queen to b6. Our plan: reroute the knight to f4, and restrict Black's c6-knight.
We play c3, clamping down on the c6-knight's advance squares.

Black's knight to e5 is aimless. Rather than rush f4, we improve patiently: the queen to c2 defends b2, connects the rooks and prepares a rook to d1 reinforcing d5; then b3 to shoo the knight when we choose, the bishop to e3 x-raying the queen, and even c4 to clamp d5 harder — unafraid of the d4-square, since bishop and rook cover it. Keep turning the screw; under steady pressure, opponents buckle.
